description: JACL Milestone 4 — Variables, Procedures & Control Flow: Add proc definitions, lexical scoping with flat frames and upvalues, if/while control flow, closures with by-value capture, and recursion

userStories.title: New opcodes for locals, jumps, calls, and closures
userStories.description: As the VM, I need new opcodes added to the OpCode enum and BytecodeChunk so that the compiler can emit instructions for local variables, control flow, procedure calls, and closures.
acceptanceCriteria: OP_GET_LOCAL added to OpCode enum — followed by uint8_t slot index
OP_SET_LOCAL added to OpCode enum — followed by uint8_t slot index
OP_GET_UPVALUE added to OpCode enum — followed by uint8_t upvalue index
OP_JUMP added to OpCode enum — followed by uint16_t forward offset
OP_JUMP_IF_FALSE added to OpCode enum — followed by uint16_t forward offset, pops condition
OP_LOOP added to OpCode enum — followed by uint16_t backward offset
OP_CALL added to OpCode enum — followed by uint8_t argument count
OP_RETURN added to OpCode enum — no operands
OP_CLOSURE added to OpCode enum — followed by uint16_t constant pool index, then N upvalue descriptors
OP_POP_N added to OpCode enum — followed by uint8_t count
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: JaclClosure struct and closure value helpers
userStories.description: As the VM and compiler, I need a closure data structure and value helpers so that procedures can be represented as first-class tagged values.
acceptanceCriteria: JaclClosure struct defined in src/value.c: BytecodeChunk chunk (compiled body), uint8_t param_count, JaclVal* param_names (inline string array), JaclVal* upvalues (captured values array), uint8_t upvalue_count, const char* name (procedure name for debug, may be NULL)
jacl_closure(JaclClosure*) constructor creates a JaclVal with JACL_TAG_CLOSURE tag and pointer payload
jacl_is_closure(JaclVal) type check returns true for closure-tagged values
jacl_as_closure(JaclVal) extracts JaclClosure* pointer from payload
All closure memory (struct, param_names array, upvalues array) is arena-allocated
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Call frames and VM execution with frames
userStories.description: As the VM, I need a call frame stack so that procedure calls save and restore execution context correctly, enabling nested and recursive calls.
acceptanceCriteria: CallFrame struct defined: JaclClosure* closure, uint8_t* return_ip, uint32_t stack_base, BytecodeChunk* chunk
VM struct has CallFrame frames[VM_FRAMES_MAX] array where VM_FRAMES_MAX is 64
VM struct has uint32_t frame_count tracking current call depth
vm_exec wraps top-level code in an implicit top-level closure/frame so all execution uses frames uniformly
OP_CALL implementation: validates arg count matches closure param_count (runtime error if mismatch), pushes new CallFrame, sets ip to closure chunk code, sets stack_base
OP_RETURN implementation: pops CallFrame, restores ip from return_ip, places return value at caller stack position, adjusts stack_top
Exceeding VM_FRAMES_MAX produces runtime error with message containing 'stack overflow'
Calling a non-closure value produces runtime error with message containing 'cannot call'
OP_GET_LOCAL pushes stack[current_frame.stack_base + slot] onto stack
OP_SET_LOCAL writes top-of-stack into stack[current_frame.stack_base + slot]
OP_GET_UPVALUE pushes current_frame.closure->upvalues[index] onto stack
OP_JUMP adds offset to ip (forward jump)
OP_JUMP_IF_FALSE pops condition, jumps if falsy (false or nil), does not jump otherwise
OP_LOOP subtracts offset from ip (backward jump)
OP_POP_N discards N values from stack top
Truthiness: false and nil are falsy, everything else (0, empty string, etc.) is truthy
Tests verify basic call/return, stack overflow error, calling non-closure error, each jump opcode
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: Compiler local variable resolution
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to resolve def bindings to local slot indices inside procedure bodies so that variable access is a fast flat-array lookup.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler tracks a Local array (name as inline string JaclVal, scope_depth as int) for each local in the current compilation scope
Compiler tracks current scope_depth, incremented when entering a block, decremented when exiting
def inside a procedure body compiles to: evaluate expr, the value occupies the local slot (no explicit SET_LOCAL needed if slot is implicit from stack position)
$x referencing a local resolves at compile time to OP_GET_LOCAL <slot_index>
def at top-level (scope_depth == 0, not inside a function) still compiles to OP_DEF_GLOBAL; $x at top level still compiles to OP_GET_GLOBAL
Exiting a scope emits OP_POP_N to clean up locals from that scope
Redefining a name in the same scope creates a new local slot (shadow, not error)
Max 256 locals per function (uint8_t slot index); exceeding produces compile error
Tests verify local resolution for simple scope, nested scopes, and shadowing
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Compile and execute if conditional
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want if/else conditional branching so that I can make decisions in my programs.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler recognizes 'if' command head
[if cond { then-body }] compiles to: compile cond, OP_JUMP_IF_FALSE over then-body, compile then-body, (push nil for else case via OP_JUMP over else + OP_NIL)
[if cond { then-body } { else-body }] compiles to: compile cond, OP_JUMP_IF_FALSE over then-body, compile then-body, OP_JUMP over else-body, compile else-body
if is an expression — returns the value of the taken branch
[if false { 1 } { 2 }] returns i32(2)
[if false { 1 }] returns nil
Nested if works: [if true { [if false { 1 } { 2 }] }] returns i32(2)
Wrong argument count (not 2 or 3 args) produces compile error
Second and third args must be AST_BLOCK or compile error
Tests verify truthy/falsy values, both branches, nesting, expression return, error cases
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: Compile and execute proc definition
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to define named procedures with proc so that I can create reusable functions.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler recognizes 'proc' command head
[proc name [params] { body }] syntax: first arg is name (AST_LIT_STRING), second is params (AST_COMMAND with bare words as args), third is body (AST_BLOCK)
proc compiles the body into a separate BytecodeChunk with its own constant pool
Parameters become local slots 0..N-1 in the new chunk
Body compilation emits OP_RETURN after the last expression (implicit return)
proc emits OP_CLOSURE to create the closure value, then OP_DEF_GLOBAL or local slot assignment to bind the name
[proc add [a b] { [+ $a $b] }] followed by [add 1 2] returns i32(3)
[proc greet [name] { [print $name] }] followed by [greet hello] prints 'hello'
Zero-parameter procedures: [proc answer [] { 42 }] then [answer] returns i32(42)
Redefining a proc name overwrites the binding
Wrong argument count for proc (not 3 args) produces compile error
Tests verify definition, invocation, parameter passing, return values, zero-params
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: Compile and execute while loop
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want a while loop so that I can perform iterative computation.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler recognizes 'while' command head
[while cond { body }] compiles to: loop-start label, compile cond, OP_JUMP_IF_FALSE to exit, compile body, OP_POP (discard body result), OP_LOOP back to loop-start
while returns nil when the loop exits
[while false { 1 }] returns nil (zero iterations)
def is allowed to rebind the same name in the same scope during while loops (pragmatic workaround for lack of mut/set! until M8)
Iterative computation test: a while loop with a counter can compute a sum (using global def rebinding)
Wrong argument count (not 2 args) produces compile error
Second arg must be AST_BLOCK or compile error
Tests verify iteration, zero-iteration, loop exit, and error cases
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: Closures and upvalue capture
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want procedures to capture variables from their enclosing scope so that I can create closures.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler tracks upvalues: when a proc body references a variable from an enclosing scope, the compiler records it as an upvalue with its source (local slot or parent upvalue index)
OP_CLOSURE instruction is followed by upvalue descriptors: for each upvalue, a (is_local, index) byte pair indicating whether to capture from the enclosing frame's locals or from its upvalues
VM OP_CLOSURE: creates JaclClosure, copies captured values into the closure's upvalue array
VM OP_GET_UPVALUE: pushes the captured value from the current closure's upvalue array
Capture is by value (snapshot at closure creation time) since all M4 bindings are immutable
[proc make-adder [x] { [proc inner [y] { [+ $x $y] }] }] — calling [make-adder 10] returns a closure, calling that with 5 returns i32(15)
Multiple closures over the same scope capture independently (modifying one does not affect the other — though values are immutable in M4 so this is automatically true)
Nested closures (3+ levels) work correctly
Tests verify capture, independent captures, nested closures
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: Recursion
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to write recursive procedures so that I can express algorithms like factorial and fibonacci.
acceptanceCriteria: A procedure can call itself by name — the proc name is bound globally before (or as) the closure is created, so the body can reference it
[proc fact [n] { [if [== $n 0] { 1 } { [* $n [fact [- $n 1]]] }] }] followed by [fact 10] returns i32(3628800)
Fibonacci works: [proc fib [n] { [if [< $n 2] { $n } { [+ [fib [- $n 1]] [fib [- $n 2]]] }] }] followed by [fib 10] returns i32(55)
Exceeding VM_FRAMES_MAX (64) produces a runtime error with 'stack overflow' in the message (catches runaway recursion)
Tests verify factorial, fibonacci, and recursion depth limit error message
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: End-to-end integration tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I need comprehensive integration tests in test/test_m4.c that exercise the full pipeline with all M4 features together.
acceptanceCriteria: test/test_m4.c exists using jacl_run() and PrintCapture pattern from test/test_integration.c
Test: [def x 10] [proc double [n] { [* $n 2] }] [print [double $x]] prints '20'
Test: factorial via recursion returns correct result for fact(10)
Test: fibonacci via recursion returns correct result for fib(10)
Test: closure captures variable from enclosing scope (make-adder pattern)
Test: if/while with various truthy/falsy values (0, nil, false, empty string, positive int)
Test: nested procedure definitions and calls
Test: error cases — wrong arg count on call, calling non-function, undefined variable inside proc body
Test: while loop computes iterative sum using def rebinding
All existing M0-M3 tests continue to pass (build.sh full suite green)
Zero memory leaks detected by tracked allocator in all tests
Test file added to build.sh TESTS array
M4 row in DESIGN.md milestone table status column updated from empty to **COMPLETE**
Commit message references M4 completion
